semantic_review.scope: Independent semantic and hygiene review of fourteen final ChainState theorems and guide; focused publication metadata/checks are separate.
review_details: Coordinate is ghost data occupying only the two polymorphic chain fields. advance preserves slot and direction and adds a Nat position. No coordinate comparison controls source admission; concrete source control, material arrays and context are retained.

Tracked preserves the complete entry and context on rejected, KDF and opening effects. Its KDF coordinate is entry.receive_chain advanced by staged skipped count. For a future opening the final coordinate advances by skipped + 1, accounting separately for the uncached target. Cached openings deliberately make no new chain-coordinate claim.

resume_tracked unfolds the existing receive resume and handles every normal source branch, including zero remaining, target exhaustion/mismatch/validation rejection, cache-slot checks and skip staging. The callback is explicitly supplied a successor coordinate and arbitrary material. The theorem does not assert that an arbitrary backend or byte-valued KDF supplies such a response.

begin_tracked follows actual admission, retains original entry/context on cached and rejected paths, and initializes a future derivation at the original receive-chain coordinate. admission_erasure reaches the actual extracted begin_receive and maps the complete effect, not only selected fields.

request_sequence needs both Aligned and the explicit source Admitted invariant; future_sequence needs Aligned, Tracked and Prepared. These are concrete operational invariants, with existing generic begin_admitted/resume_admitted facts available, not hidden cryptographic assumptions. The guide does not claim them for arbitrary dynamic-world states.

Counter arithmetic agrees with Rust: send at U64.MAX is exhausted unchanged, admitted send increments mathematically by one, target/skipped receive increments use checked source transitions, and successful U8 skip addition is related to Nat addition through UScalar.add_equiv. Nat ghost advancement is not a wraparound model; impossible exhausted/future combinations are excluded by source control or explicit operational invariants.

failed_open identifies the entire labeled kernel with the original entry for an absent opening response, including both chains, control and all cached material. failed_open_retry proves identical fresh admission on that returned kernel for the same target/context. Neither theorem rolls back an external random table or claims an entire retry trace/table coherence proof.

SendTracked records unchanged receive counter/cache and exact send increment on admitted requests. send_ready_kernel identifies the complete advanced kernel, preserving receive chain and receive slots. send_ready_aligned establishes both counter alignments before sealing. The documented failed-seal advancement is inherited from the existing source program and matches concrete SendSeal.finish.

erase uses arbitrary chains : Coordinate Slot -> RatchetChain with no injectivity premise. resume_erasure preserves the complete interpreted pending effect with an explicit mapped typed response. The theorem does not discharge primitive-backend coherence, full76 parsing, or a complete concrete-response/source-game simulation.

The same initial coordinates are shared by counterpart directions: false/position1 is Server send and Beacon receive; true/position0 is Beacon send and Server receive. Seed erasure binds these coordinates to next32/right32 respectively and equates complete kernels to the integrated Seed constructors. seeds_aligned proves both constructors total and aligned.

Skipped cache entries retain the original arbitrary Material payloads. No theorem identifies them with persistent lazy-table coordinates, proves successful receive publication/consumption across the dynamic world, or establishes alias probabilities. The guide expressly lists these remaining joins.

No new cryptographic premise, fixed independent family, freshness/injectivity assumption, source-origin assertion or security/resource bound appears. Guide accurately limits this to an operational R3 component and distinguishes persistent table/compiler and evolving-chain security work.
